 ii) river rapture may occur by headward extension of the long profile
  This happens when rivers are sharing a watershed
  The actively eroding river gradually cuts back its slope head until it encroaches upon the the
 divide or water shed of the other river
  Eventually the power reaches the source of the weaker river and diverts its water into its
 chanell
  River rapture may also ocuur where there are two adjacent rivers
  One of the rivers has more erosive power than the other
  The more powerfull river erodes away the ridge that separates the two by head ward erosion
  Eventually it encroaches into the valley of the weaker river diverting its waters into its valleys
